chunks: My father, Allah may have mercy upon him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Hubab al-Wasiti from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is very ugly for a believer to be humiliated by his desires.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to be humiliated by their desires?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this saying of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to define the spiritual stature of the true believer, linking inner self-mastery to external dignity. The Imam teaches that uncontrolled desire (*shahwah*) acts as a master that humiliates the soul, a concept deeply rooted in the Shia tradition of *nafs* purification. This serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain their honor by subduing base impulses rather than being enslaved by them.
